reason: Lens 2 (cards and rulings): no verified refutation stands after round 3. My round-3 counterexample (801.16 / 104.4e: a player for whom the game was a draw leaves without losing, and the stipulation would have made that player the first loser) was answered by a fix in the rule text. The rule now applies only when the game was won by one player and no player left because the game was a draw for them, and any game that was a draw for any player goes by the draw sentence of 103.1; the verifier passed the answers with nothing standing. The derivation holds: step 1 (103.1 gives the choice to 'the loser of the previous game') and step 4 (draw sentence untouched) are sourced and say no more than their quotes. Step 2 (800.4) is used only for players being out at different times, and F2 supplies that they lost. Step 3 is a stipulation filling a gap: 103.1 says only 'the loser' and no card ruling or CR text says which of several losers chooses. The 800.4h point does not apply because the 103.1 chooser acts at the start of the next game. I accept the stipulation as the rule: the first loser chooses; simultaneous first losers agree among themselves, else random; draws, team games and games whose start the CR already settles (103.1b Archenemy, 904.12c Supervillain Rumble) are left alone. The deeming of players still in the game as losers closes the won-by-effect gap, and the carve-out for draws or limited-range-of-influence draws removes the 104.5 conflict. I know of no card or ruling that contradicts it.

evidence.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.
If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.
If a player loses the game, that player leaves the game. If the game is a draw for a player, that player leaves the game.
As in a normal Free-for-All game, the starting player is randomly determined.
